title: A new risk assessment model of venous thromboembolism by considering fuzzy population.
summary: The open-access primary article develops a fuzzy-population VTE risk model on 3,284 PUMCH inpatients and compares it with five ML baselines and Padua scoring; the held-out temporal test reports higher specificity at equal sensitivity.
ai_technology: The proposed ML model operationalizes fuzzy-population splitting for VTE risk assessment.
organization: Not stated in the abstract reviewed

evidence.tested: On the temporal test set the model reaches 64.94% specificity and 90.24% sensitivity, compared with Padua 63.30% and 90.24%.
evidence.unknown: The admission-time split provides held-out validation and comparator checks, bounded to this inpatient cohort.
evidence.ai_role: The proposed ML model operationalizes fuzzy-population splitting for VTE risk assessment.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
